title: Metabolic, haematological and infective bone disease

steps.tx: **Paget disease** of bone progresses through osteolytic, mixed, and osteosclerotic phases. Radiographs demonstrate the advancing **blade of grass** sign (candle-flame sign) in long bones, cortical thickening, coarsened trabeculae, and skeletal expansion, accompanied by a 1% risk of malignant osteosarcoma transformation.
steps.say: Paget disease of bone is known to progress through osteolytic, mixed, and osteosclerotic phases. Radiographs demonstrate the advancing blade of grass sign, also called candle-flame sign, in long bones, cortical thickening, coarsened trabeculae, and skeletal expansion, accompanied by a 1% risk of malignant osteosarcoma transformation.

steps.tx: Chronic **Hyperparathyroidism** triggers severe osteoclastic resorption throughout the skeleton, causing pathognomonic subperiosteal bone resorption on the radial aspect of the middle phalanges of the 2nd and 3rd fingers. Additional manifestations include the **rugger-jersey spine** with sclerotic endplates and expansile osteolytic brown tumours.

right.title: Brown Tumour Characteristics
points: Contain haemosiderin, giant cells, and fibrous tissue
Appear hypermetabolic on PET and bone scans

steps.tx: **Renal osteodystrophy** in chronic kidney disease is seen to combine osteomalacia, secondary hyperparathyroidism, and osteosclerosis into a complex skeletal syndrome. Radiographs demonstrate soft tissue vascular calcification, subchondral bone resorption, rugger-jersey spine, and massive periarticular lobulated calcific masses known as **tumoral calcinosis**.

rows: Enhanced osteoid synthesis stimulated by PTH

steps.tx: **Fibrous dysplasia** is a benign congenital medullary lesion where normal bone is replaced by immature fibro-osseous tissue. Radiographs classically display a hazy ground-glass matrix with a thick rind of sclerosis, which weakens the proximal femur and causes the pathognomonic **shepherd crook** varus deformity.

steps.tx: In **Sickle cell anaemia**, bone radiography displays marked compensatory erythroid marrow hyperplasia with a classical hair-on-end calvarial appearance. Microvascular bone infarction of central vertebral growth plates produces characteristic **H-shaped vertebrae** with central endplate depression, while functional asplenia predisposes to avascular necrosis and invasive salmonella osteomyelitis.

rows: Microvascular ischemia of central growth plates (Reynold sign)
Salmonella infection facilitated by functional asplenia

steps.tx: A **Bone infarction** demonstrates a serpiginous, calcified sclerotic margin on plain radiography across the metaphysis or diaphysis. On T2-weighted MRI, osteonecrosis exhibits the pathognomonic **double-line sign**, consisting of an outer hypointense rim representing sclerotic bone and an inner hyperintense rim representing vascularized granulation tissue.

left.title: Double-Line Sign on MRI
points: Outer hypointense rim: Sclerotic reactive bone
Inner hyperintense rim: Hypervascular granulation tissue
Highly specific for avascular necrosis on T2 MRI
Separates necrotic core from viable marrow
Seen in femoral head and metadiaphyseal infarcts

right.title: Radiographic Appearance
points: Spares joint space when located in diaphysis
Subchondral crescent sign indicates articular collapse
Associated with steroid use, alcohol, and sickle cell

steps.tx: Subacute and chronic **osteomyelitis** exhibits characteristic radiological signatures of chronicity including the **sequestrum**, an island of necrotic devitalized bone separated from viable tissue. The surrounding reactive periosteal bone forms the involucrum, while cortical cloaca defects permit persistent drainage of infected purulent material.

rows: Loss of blood supply creates necrotic intraosseous nidus
Thick sleeve of new periosteal cortical bone
Subperiosteal osteoblastic response walling off infection
Defect or opening in the involucrum
Draining sinus tract venting pus and debris to soft tissues

steps.tx: **Haemophilic arthropathy** develops secondary to recurrent intra-articular haemarthrosis during childhood. Synovial haemosiderin deposition stimulates chronic inflammatory pannus and hyperaemia, causing epiphyseal overgrowth, squaring of the inferior pole of the patella, and marked widening and deepening of the femoral **intercondylar notch**.
